title: Comparison of Primary Implant Stability and Stem Migration of the EXCIA T® Hip Stem Using Different Generations of Broaches
summary:
This study compares two different instruments (Broaches) used during the implantation of the EXCIA T® hip prosthesis.
The aim is to investigate whether the newer generation of rasps contributes to a more stable initial fixation of the hip prosthesis in the bone and whether it reduces early postoperative subsidence or migration of the femoral stem compared with the previous generation of rasps.
The results of this study are intended to help further optimize the surgical technique and improve the long-term stability of the hip prosthesis.
conditions: Degenerative hip osteoarthritis (coxarthrosis), Rheumatoid arthritis of the hip joint, Femoral head osteonecrosis (avascular necrosis of the femoral head)

interventions.name:
The present study is a non-interventional, monocentric retrospective-prospective comparative study. Two patient cohorts with EXCIA T® hip prostheses (n = 49 each) will be analyzed with regard to primary implant stability and stem migration behavior (subsidence) after 12 months.

Forty-nine patients treated with the third generation of broach (retrospective cohort with prospective data collection).
The study is investigator-initiated and will be conducted using a 1:1 matching design.
